title: The filter-traffic doc's evaluation order lists five exclusion kinds; the code evaluates seven, and the two undocumented ones silently block traffic
statement: filter-traffic.mdx says Rybbit checks exclusions in this order and lists IP, country, path, hostname, user agent, then notes that a match makes the event return 200 while not being tracked. The exclusion decision actually evaluates seven kinds, adding ASN and query parameter, and neither filter-traffic.mdx nor site-settings.mdx mentions query-parameter exclusions anywhere. A configured query-param exclusion therefore drops traffic exactly as the doc's closing sentence promises, for a kind the doc's own list does not name.

handVerified.note: Report section 8, both halves, and it corrects the corpus upward: the doc omits TWO kinds, not one. Site 37, PUT /config declaring excludedQueryParams ['preview'] returns 200 and GET /excluded-query-params reads it back. PROBE POST /api/track with querystring '?preview=1' returns 200 {"success":true,"message":"Event not tracked - query param excluded"}; CONTROL POST /api/track with '?utm_source=x' returns a plain 200 {"success":true}. The board scenario fails at step 3 on exactly that message.

source.howDecided: git log 613cd015..HEAD on both files returns nothing. At HEAD filter-traffic.mdx:120-130 still lists exactly five kinds under '## How Filters Are Evaluated', and siteExclusionDecision.ts still evaluates seven in order: IP (:168), ASN (:171-183), country (:185-195), path (:200), query param (:203-208), hostname (:211), user agent (:222). The module's own type declares all seven (SiteExclusionReason at :40 is "ip" | "asn" | "country" | "path" | "query_param" | "hostname" | "user_agent") and its doc comment at :154 spells the same order out in prose.

queries: gh api --paginate 'repos/rybbit-io/rybbit/issues?state=all&per_page=100' (not a search; 1044 items, 320 non-PR issues, numbers 1 to 1131 with 87 gaps) then a local regex scan of every issue title plus body

local regex over all 320 issues: query param|excludedQueryParams|ASN  ->  10 hits, all matching on unrelated uses of 'param' (#1034, #1008, #939, #922, #898, #856, #842, #731, #184, #137); none is about exclusion kinds

reevaluation: The finding stands, source untouched, still unreported. Re-verification strengthens one detail: the gap is not just between prose and behaviour, it is between two files in the same repo, because siteExclusionDecision.ts:40 and its doc comment at :154 both enumerate all seven kinds in the same order the doc gets wrong, so the correct list already exists in-repo and only has to be copied across. Severity is low but the shape is unusually clean for a doc issue: the undocumented kind does not fail loudly, it silently discards traffic while returning 200, which is precisely the behaviour a self-hoster would spend a long time misdiagnosing if they had inherited a config with a query-param exclusion in it. The corpus scenario is a deliberate red rather than an accidental one, so the board is not evidence of surprise, only of the mismatch.
notes: Report section 8 (a deliberate red; the report gives it no F id). Doc-side finding. The docs live in this same repo under docs/content/docs, so there is no separate docs repo and no 'docs repo issue' route: a doc fix here is a one-line PR against rybbit-io/rybbit. Five of the ten findings (R6, R7, R8, R9, R10) are doc-side. Filing five separate doc issues would burn maintainer patience for little gain; consider one consolidated 'documentation does not match behaviour' issue listing all five with file and line, or a single PR. Body should be the doc's five-item list next to the code's seven, then the probe and control on /api/track showing a silently dropped event with a 200. Lead with query parameters rather than ASN: query-param exclusions are configurable through the API and are the ones a user will actually hit, whereas ASN is a narrower audience. Point at siteExclusionDecision.ts:40 and :154 as the authoritative list, which makes the fix a copy rather than a research task. rybbit-io/rybbit applies NO labels: all 40 most recent issues carry an empty label array, and both templates declare labels: ''. Do not add a 'Suggested labels' line here; there is no vocabulary to copy and it would only add noise. The bug template is a classic markdown template with bold headers (**Describe the bug**, **To Reproduce**, **Expected behavior**, **Screenshots**, **Desktop**, **Smartphone**, **Additional context**), not a YAML form, and no template-enforcing workflow exists, so there is no auto-close bot to trip.
